answer.rationale: The p99 latency spike of 5x target correlates temporally with the release 2 hours ago. Memory_b1 demonstrates that rollback cleared a checkout error spike without customer impact on a stable prior build. Memory_b6 shows staged release gating catches regressions quickly. Verifying both confirms rollback success patterns and that the prior build was stable. At settlement peak with heavy writes, a bad release is the highest-probability root cause. Rollback is lower-latency than capacity provisioning (memory_b3 precedent requires lead time) and more targeted than regional failover (memory_b2 is for regional degradation, not post-release spike). Circuit breakers (memory_b4) protect dependent paths but don't address write path latency. Route read replicas (memory_b5) reduces dashboard load but doesn't help transactional writes under peak settlement load. Rollback preserves the option to re-release with fixes while stopping customer impact now. If the release is not the cause, the next window can pursue capacity or failover.
